catalogue_requests.reason: No catalogue class fits one raw geometry_msgs/Twist publication. cap.motion.mobile_base.v1 requires duration_s and returns measured distance_m, heading_rad and stopped, while the gz-sim DiffDrive plugin consumes the published Twist and publishes no completion acknowledgement. This binding sets only linear.x and angular.z; a rosbridge publication receipt is transmission evidence only.
No catalogue class observes simulation time. cap.world.step.v1, cap.world.reset.v1 and cap.world.seed.v1 act on a world; none subscribes to /clock or carries a rosgraph_msgs/Clock sample.

No catalogue class carries a sensor_msgs/JointState observation. cap.motion.joint_position.v1 is an invoke class that commands joint positions and requires an acknowledged motion, not a passive joint-name/position/velocity sample.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Confirmed the author's block: the clone creates no ROS service or action server, the only command surface is the bridged /cmd_vel Twist that the gz DiffDrive plugin consumes (ros_gz_bridge.yaml:17-21, gazebo.xacro:183-216), and both the README's and AMRController's stop are single zero-Twist publications (README.md:1921-1923, amr_menu.py:50-54), so no acknowledged stop exists and the gate fails only G6.ESTOP_FAILED and G8 SAFE-028. Checked every endpoint and type, the Odometry pose.pose and twist.twist read paths, the Clock and JointState mappings, the launch files, the fake, the tests and all 13 facts against the pin. The two velocity limits were one-sided Limit(max=2.0) cited to the DiffDrive clamps, which left every reverse or negative command unbounded (a reviewer probe published linear.x -1000 m/s and angular.z -1000 rad/s as completed); the reviewer made both operator_required with an example overlay (driver.py, new site-limits.example.json), replaced the envelope test with cases for both signs and for the refusal without an overlay (test_driver.py), rewrote the joint-state bridge fact to name the Gazebo topic and added five facts (the JointStatePublisher declared without a topic, whose comment names /world/*/model/*/joint_state while the bridge reads /joint_states; robot.launch.py starting joint_state_publisher_gui through display.launch.py; and the licence conflict of an MIT LICENSE with Apache-2.0 in package.xml) and two gaps, updated facts.md, and regenerated reference.json, REFERENCE.md and check-report.json. The gate still fails exactly G6 and G8 SAFE-028 with the stable digest unchanged (sha256:9a96c514f36339a071c81168ad1c100de072388458dd301ef646b6a6346fcfd0; RESULT.json quotes the run-specific report digest), the eight package cases pass, and the LIMITS paragraph of the author's RESULT.json notes (only the 'sourced' positive 2.0 maxima declared) is superseded: both inputs are now operator_required. For the human reviewer: Simulated differential-drive AMR in Gazebo Harmonic (R2 kept as the author chose, like other mobile-base simulators). No stop exists in the clone: /cmd_vel is a plain bridged topic, nothing in the clone zeroes a stale command, and the README and AMRController stop by publishing one zero Twist. Unblocking needs an acknowledged stop (the clone bridges no Gazebo world-control service) or an SDK profile for a fenced zero-velocity stop with a sensed standstill. amr_menu.py and drive_pattern.py are further /cmd_vel publishers. In robot.launch.py, joint_state_publisher_gui publishes slider values on /joint_states, and the gz JointStatePublisher output probably never reaches the bridge, so live joint-state reads are unreliable. Licence conflict inside the clone: MIT LICENSE versus Apache-2.0 in package.xml, while the card says publish_review not_required; the owner decides.
